speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if you've experienced any recent weight changes or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

Do you have a family history of breast or ovarian cancer, and have you noticed any pleural effusion or ascites on recent imaging?
REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen and Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of ascites, pleural effusion, and an ovarian mass, I suspect Meigs syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Diagnostic Thoracentesis

speaker: Doctor
text: The transudative nature of the effusion and the ovarian mass strongly support a diagnosis of Meigs syndrome. To confirm the benign nature of the mass and rule out malignancy, I need to see the imaging directly. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT scan rules out malignancy, and the transudative effusion confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs syndrome
